name: The Merrion
positioning: Five-star hotel made from four restored Georgian townhouses in the heart of Georgian Dublin, opposite Government Buildings
best_for: Travelers who want a historic Georgian base within walking distance of Dublin's galleries, museums and Grafton Street
Guests who value art, period interiors and formal gardens

facts.text: The Merrion is a restoration of four Georgian townhouses.
The four townhouses were built in 1756 on Upper Merrion Street.
The hotel is in the heart of Georgian Dublin, opposite Government Buildings.
The hotel is a few minutes' walk from galleries, museums, the Dublin Convention Centre and the shops of Grafton Street.
Merrion Square and the National Gallery of Ireland are a short walk away.
The Merrion is a member of The Leading Hotels of the World.
Rooms and suites are in the historic Main House and in the Garden Wing, where traditional meets contemporary.
Bathrooms are spacious, with Carrara marble, deep tubs and walk-in showers.
The main stairwell is lined with neoclassical murals by Martin Mooney.
The Spa and Health Club, below the Garden Wing, is open 7 days a week.
The Cellar Bar is set in the original 18th-century wine vaults of the Main House.
A la carte breakfast in The Garden Room is included for all guests.

highlights.text: The Merrion houses one of Ireland's most significant private collections of contemporary art, displayed throughout its public spaces.
Its two formal gardens were created by landscape designer Jim Reynolds to evoke an 18th-century estate.
The interiors were designed by Alice Roden, a local designer and weaver.
The Lord Antrim and Lord Monck Suites offer separate living and dining areas and fireplaces.
Afternoon Tea is served year-round in the Drawing Rooms, which have open log fires.

considerations.text: Guests must be over 18 for spa treatments.
The Garden Terrace is enjoyed during the spring and summer months.
Restaurant Patrick Guilbaud is on the property but operated separately, and booking ahead is essential.
